# Demo: estimate follow-up

<!-- Generated by docs/demo/generate_estimate_followup.py. Do not edit by hand;
     change the skill, config, or fixture and re-run the generator. -->

A walkthrough of the `estimate-followup` example skill
(`deploy/skills/workflow-intelligence-examples/estimate-followup/`) on its shipped
fixture. Nothing below is typed by hand: the settings and the fixture table
are read from the shipped files, and the call log, the Telegram message, the
ledger, and the JSON come from running the skill's CLI. The generator script
named above rewrites this file, and the skill's tests fail if it falls out of
date.

The business is a made-up roofing company, Example Ridge Roofing. All names, addresses,
phone numbers (555-01xx), and emails (example.com, example.net) are fake.

## Setup

The run is pinned to Monday 2026-11-02 so it is reproducible. The relevant
settings from `config.toml`:

```toml
[selection]
followup_after_days = 3
max_followups = 2
redraft_after_days = 3
max_drafts_per_run = 6

[business]
name = "Example Ridge Roofing"
sender_name = "Jordan"
timezone = "America/Denver"
```

The voice templates are in the same file, under `[voice]`.

## The run

The generator serves the fixture with `scripts/fixture_server.py` and points
the skill at it, so this run goes through the real HTTP client, the same
path a fork's CRM would use. The command is the pulse's command plus
`--source`, `--today`, `--state`, and `-v` (log each call):

```bash
python3 scripts/estimate_followup.py --format telegram --record \
  --source http://127.0.0.1:PORT --today 2026-11-02 --state /tmp/.../surfaced.json -v
```

Source calls (stderr). Call 1 lists open estimate IDs; call 2 reads each one:

```text
source: GET /estimates?status=open -> 200
source: GET /estimates/EST-2041 -> 200
source: GET /estimates/EST-2042 -> 200
source: GET /estimates/EST-2043 -> 200
source: GET /estimates/EST-2044 -> 200
source: GET /estimates/EST-2045 -> 200
source: GET /estimates/EST-2046 -> 200
source: GET /estimates/EST-2047 -> 200
source: GET /estimates/EST-2049 -> 200
source: GET /estimates/EST-2050 -> 200
source: GET /estimates/EST-2051 -> 200
source: GET /estimates/EST-2053 -> 200
source: GET /estimates/EST-2054 -> 200
```

```text
[5/5] EST-2042 · Sam Sample · $2,340 gutter replacement
22 Sample St, Sampleton
Sent Oct 30 (3 days ago), no reply. First follow-up.
Text to 555-0102

Hi Sam, it's Jordan with Example Ridge Roofing. Checking in on the gutter replacement estimate from Oct 30. Any questions, or want to get on the schedule? Pricing holds through Nov 29.

Needs a fix in the CRM:
- EST-2046 Morgan Mockup: no usable email or phone on file
- EST-2054 Drew Dataless: bad data, sent_at is missing

Not drafted: 1 do-not-contact, 1 replied, 1 expired, 1 follow-up limit reached, 1 not due yet.

Nothing has been sent. Reply "edit 2: ..." to change a draft. Send the ones you approve from your own inbox or phone.
```

The operator reads this, edits any draft by replying (for example "edit 2:
mention we can start the week of the 16th"), and sends the ones they approve
from their own inbox or phone. That reply loop is the agent rewriting a
draft under the rules in SKILL.md; it is model output, not deterministic, so
it is not reproduced here. For replies to reach the agent with the drafts in
context, turn on continuable cron deliveries (see
`workspace-docs/HEARTBEAT.md`).

### Why each estimate landed where it did

| ID | Outcome |
|----|---------|
| EST-2041 | Draft #1 (email, 6 days, follow-up 1) |
| EST-2042 | Draft #5 (sms, 3 days, follow-up 1) |
| EST-2043 | Draft #2 (email, 5 days, follow-up 2, last one) |
| EST-2044 | Skipped: replied (customer replied 2026-10-28) |
| EST-2045 | Skipped: expired (expired 2026-10-24) |
| EST-2046 | Flagged for the operator: no usable email or phone on file |
| EST-2047 | Skipped: not due yet (2 days since last touch) |
| EST-2048 | Not listed by call 1 (status won) |
| EST-2049 | Skipped: follow-up limit reached (2 follow-ups already sent) |
| EST-2050 | Skipped: do-not-contact |
| EST-2051 | Draft #3 (email, 5 days, follow-up 1) |
| EST-2052 | Not listed by call 1 (status lost) |
| EST-2053 | Draft #4 (email, 4 days, follow-up 1) |
| EST-2054 | Flagged for the operator: bad data, sent_at is missing |

## Second run the same morning

The first run recorded what it put in front of the operator:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "surfaced": {
    "EST-2041": "2026-11-02",
    "EST-2042": "2026-11-02",
    "EST-2043": "2026-11-02",
    "EST-2046": "2026-11-02",
    "EST-2051": "2026-11-02",
    "EST-2053": "2026-11-02",
    "EST-2054": "2026-11-02"
  }
}
```

Run again with the same ledger and nothing is new (everything surfaced is
inside the 3-day redraft window), so the output is the marker that tells
Hermes cron to deliver nothing:

```text
[SILENT]
```

## What the agent sees on a chat preview

When the operator asks in chat ("which estimates need a follow-up?"), the
agent runs `--format json` without `--record`, so the preview never
changes what the next pulse sends. Draft #1 from a fresh run, as JSON:

```json
{
  "n": 1,
  "estimate_id": "EST-2041",
  "customer": "Pat Placeholder",
  "channel": "email",
  "to": "pat.placeholder@example.com",
  "days_waiting": 6,
  "followup_number": 1,
  "is_final": false,
  "previously_surfaced_on": null,
  "subject": "Checking in on your roof replacement estimate",
  "body": "Hi Pat,\n\nJust checking in on the roof replacement estimate I sent over on Oct 27. Happy to walk through any line of it, adjust the scope, or get you on the schedule. Pricing holds through Nov 26.\n\nThanks,\nJordan\nExample Ridge Roofing | 555-0142"
}
```

```bash
python3 docs/demo/generate_estimate_followup.py
```
